newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Cambodia to hold elections next May, Hun Sen says.
newsitem.headline: Cambodia to hold elections next May, Hun Sen says.

text.p: Cambodia's Second Prime Minister Hun Sen, who ousted his co-premier in a bloody takeover last week, said on Tuesday that elections would be held next May.

"My party is like any other party and I hope on May 23, 1998, there will be an election and the election will be free, fair and right," the second prime minister told Voice of America's Khmer language service.
Hun Sen ousted his coalition government partner, First Prime Minister Prince Norodom Ranariddh, on July 6 after two days of battles in Phnom Penh.
Hun Sen said he thought relations with the United States, which suspended aid for 30 days in response to Ranariddh's ouster, were steady.
"I think this relationship is not changeable and the suspension of aid for one month, I think it's not so bad," he said.
Hun Sen and Ranariddh agreed last month that Cambodia's next election would be on May 23, the fifth anniversary of a U.N.-supervised election which Ranariddh's royalist party won.
Hun Sen said he was following a democratic path.
"I would like to inform that democracy is being implemented in the country," he told the radio station.
He said steps were under way to chose a new first prime minister to replace Ranariddh and the national assembly would sit again on July 28.

A row over dissident members of Ranariddh's FUNCINPEC party crippled the two prime ministers' coalition government. Earlier this year, bitter disagreement over how to handle the splintering Khmer Rouge guerrilla group strained the two men's already icy relations.
Hun Sen justified his overthrow of Ranariddh by saying the prince was smuggling defectors from the Khmer Rouge into the capital to strengthen his forces.
Ranariddh, who was abroad when Hun Sen's forces moved against the prince's troops in Phnom Penh on July 5, has vowed to resist Hun Sen's takeover of power.

Troops loyal to the prince have been pushed back into northern jungle and his royalist party has been left in disarray, with many members choosing exile after Ranariddh's ouster and the killing of at least two senior royalists.
